subject: Initialize: Enterprise access controls walkthrough and runbook
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-telecom.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-telecom.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initialize: Enterprise access controls walkthrough and runbook

Hi Samantha / Jordan —

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to share a concise plan for the access-control portion of your Redwood onboarding: SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, IP allowlist windows, and service-account provisioning. I attached a short runbook and a SCIM mapping template that should make the first week predictable.

High-level timing (proposed):
- Day 0: Account provisioning & org-level policy review (you provide admin owners)
- Day 1: SAML integration (test IdP connection, confirm attributes)
- Day 2: SCIM pilot (provision a small group, validate attributes)
- Day 3: IP allowlist cutoff & service-account creation for automation
- Day 4: Cutover rehearsal and rollback plan

Open questions we should lock before SAML test:
- Which attribute will you use as the canonical username (email / uid)?
- Any downstream systems that need alternate emails mapped?
- Do you have a preferred schedule for the IP allowlist switch (UTC window)?

Attached: redwood-access-runbook-v1.2.pdf (runbook), scim-mapping-template.xlsx (mapping), service-account-provisioning-instructions.md

Next actions: can you confirm the IdP admin contact and a preferred time for the SAML test (we recommend a morning window to allow rollback same day)? I'll coordinate an hour block and a short pre-check call.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-access-runbook-v1.2.pdf, scim-mapping-template.xlsx, service-account-provisioning-instructions.md

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-telecom.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-telecom.com>, it-ops@acme-telecom.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initialize: Enterprise access controls walkthrough and runbook

Diego —

Thanks, this looks great and clear. Quick answers to the open questions:
- Canonical username: work_email (we want email as the primary identifier)
- We do have a legacy helpdesk that uses user_id; will need SCIM mapping for that field too (I attached internal note).
- IP allowlist: prefer a 00:00–02:00 UTC window on a weekday (Thu/Fri work for us).

IdP admin: Jordan Price (cc'd) will be the contact and can do the SAML test next Thursday morning (our time).

Two asks before the SAML test:
1) Can you confirm the exact SAML attribute names Redwood expects for email, firstName, lastName, and groups?
2) For SCIM pilot, can you outline how group-to-role mapping will be represented in the mapping template?

We'll also need a service-account naming convention for automation bots so our security team can pre-approve them.

Samantha Ortiz
Director, IT Operations | Acme Telecom
Samantha Ortiz | Acme Telecom

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-telecom.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-telecom.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initialize: Enterprise access controls walkthrough and runbook

Samantha — thanks for the quick answers. Below are the explicit attribute names and the mapping approach. I've also called out the service-account naming convention we recommend.

SAML attribute expectations (Redwood):
- email -> eduPersonPrincipalName or mail (we accept either but prefer mail)
- firstName -> givenName
- lastName -> sn
- groups -> memberOf (SCIM will map groups to roles; SAML group claim optional)

SCIM mapping approach (see attached template):
- Map SCIM attributes to Redwood fields: userName -> email, name.givenName -> firstName, name.familyName -> lastName, externalId -> user_id
- For legacy helpdesk: map externalId to helpdesk_user_id and include a custom attribute helpdesk_id in the pilot CSV
- Group-to-role mapping: SCIM group displayName -> Redwood role name. We'll stage this in the template tab "role-mapping" and run a dry-provision for a 10-user pilot before bulk sync.

Service-account naming convention (recommended):
- Format: redwood-svc-<team>-<purpose>-<env> (e.g. redwood-svc-monitoring-bot-prod)
- We will tag service accounts with an "owner" and "lifetime" to satisfy your security team's review.

IP allowlist window: we can schedule the 00:00–02:00 UTC window on Thursday, May 27. We'll run pre-checks the day before and provide a rollback plan.

I'll schedule the SAML test for Thu May 27 00:30 UTC (your morning). Marissa, Neha and Karthik — I'm looping you for technical backup and the SCIM pilot run.

Regards,

Diego Fernandez
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachments: role-mapping: scim-mapping-template.xlsx (role-mapping tab)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-telecom.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initialize: Enterprise access controls walkthrough and runbook

Looping in the implementation team.

Quick notes from an implementation perspective:
- We'll run the SCIM pilot against a sandbox org (no PII) and provide a delta report after the dry run.
- Karthik will own the service-account provisioning and will provide a terraform snippet and a naming-enforcement script.
- Neha will validate org-policy settings (password/2FA enforcement, token lifetimes) and will share a short checklist by EOD Monday.

Samantha: we'll prepare a short run of the provisioning job and a sample rollback (remove provisioned users) so your IT security team can review change logs. If you want, we can run a pre-check call Wed (May 26) UTC morning to walk the team through the SCIM mapping tab and the service-account naming policy.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Senior Implementation Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: service-account-provisioning-instructions.md
